written: 2026-10-01 afternoon, after the stripe code was found (Amendment 5, ed44991) and before its phases, relay or ring-segment counterfactuals were run
status: CONFIRMATORY for the predictions below (criteria fixed before the runs); the ring-segment counterfactuals' controls are part of them. Anything computed beyond them is labelled exploratory.
question: How is the stripe built after the ring is released, and which of the face's mechanisms transfer? The face was written in four phases (flood, clear, write, latch) by a loop between the ring, the background and the face parts, with a second rise of the conductance latching it, and no part of the ring wrote it alone.
subject: The stripe code: order 2, restart 6 of the ceiling-2 pilot (data/boundaryHarmonicTraining1888Hold301StripesInteriorMinus60Minus5Ceiling2/order2_restart06.npz): a0 = 1.350, a1 = 0.0012, a2 = 0.1373, ring values 1.21 to 1.49, best moment recorded iteration 504, balanced score 8.922 mV, overlap 1.000. Model 1888, hold 301.
registeredBefore: the record, branch and switch-rule runs on that code, the relay decomposition of it, and the ring-segment counterfactuals of it. ALREADY SEEN: every face result; for the stripes, the training tables, the code and its pattern at the best moment (all 27 stripe cells dark, no strays), and the registered replays S7 and S8 of that code (the field off leaves no interior cell dark, so S7 holds; holding the ring for the whole run also reaches overlap 1.000, at iteration 472, so S8 fails); and, from an EARLIER, DIFFERENT code (order 2, a0 = 0.949, a2 = 0.558, overlap 0.852, best moment 488), a trajectory in which the stripe forms during the first collapse of the conductance and lasts 74 iterations, a relay in which the field carries ring top to stripe upper and ring bottom to stripe lower in flood and clear, and ring-segment counterfactuals in which the top and bottom rows alone gave 90% of the full effect and the six cells facing the stripe's ends 74%. NOT SEEN: the stripe code's own trajectory, switch-rule fit, relay or counterfactuals.

definitions.stripeCells: the 27 centre-stripe cells (interior rows 1-9, columns 4-6); flankCells: the 54 interior cells in columns 1-3 and 7-9; dark: Vmem < -34.6 mV
definitions.selectivity: mean G_pol / G_ref over the stripe cells minus the mean over the flank cells, at the best moment (iteration 504)
definitions.bestMoment: recorded iteration 504, the scored moment, which is also the relay's primary readout (no second rise is assumed)
definitions.trough: the iteration of the lowest interior mean conductance between iterations 302 and 1300 of the stripe code's 3000-iteration run
definitions.relayBaseline: extraUpdateOnly, as for the face: the clamp's tissue-wide extra Vmem update in the hold, but the ring never held; decomposed by computeBoundaryHarmonicRelay11x11.py --target stripesInterior --order 2
definitions.blocks: the ten-block layout (boundaryHarmonicCoarseGrain.stripeRegionLabels): ring top, bottom, left, right; stripe upper and lower; each flank upper and lower; a left and a right block are mirror images, so the left ones and the centre ones are read
definitions.netTransfer: relayLoopNets.readNet: the block net of the field channel (and of the contact channel) summed over the windows of a phase, positive along a pair's canonical direction (the earlier block in ringTop, ringBottom, ringLeft, stripeUpper, stripeLower, flankLeftUpper, flankLeftLower to the later one). Phases: flood = the windows inside the hold; clear = from the hold to the best moment (the stripe code is read before any second rise, so the write phase is empty if the trough is after the best moment)

V1.criterion: one-step closure <= 1e-6 at every step and every readout's flux conserved to <= 1e-3 relative after the hold (the face's own tolerances)

V2.claim: the replay reproduces the stored code
V2.criterion: the stripe code replayed single-sample reproduces its training score and best moment to within 1e-6 mV

V3.claim: the left and right blocks are mirror images
V3.criterion: the block net is left-right symmetric to <= 1e-4 of its largest transfer

predictions.name: P1-theSwitchRuleHolds
predictions.basis: face: 99.1-99.6% one-step accuracy across all seven trained codes; the rule is derived from the model's constants
predictions.claim: the latching-switch rule describes the stripe code as well
predictions.criterion: one-step accuracy >= 0.99 for the stripe code from iteration 0 to its best moment, and >= 0.99 for the best code of every other size in the ceiling-2 pilot (orders 0, 1, 3)

predictions.name: P2-theStripeFormsInTheFirstCollapse
predictions.basis: CONTRAST with the face, which was scored on the second rise (trough 585, second peak 1765, scored 2173); the earlier 0.852 code formed its stripe before its trough
predictions.claim: the stripe is not a second-rise latch: it is scored before the interior mean conductance has turned
predictions.criterion: the stripe code's best moment (504) is earlier than its trough

predictions.name: P3-theStripeCellsHoldTheirConductance
predictions.basis: face: the second rise lifts the face's cells 0.356 above the rest
predictions.claim: at the best moment the stripe cells hold more conductance than the flank cells

predictions.name: P4-theFlanksRelight
predictions.basis: the earlier code's flanks fell through the bottom of the switching window first while the stripe cells stayed dark
predictions.claim: what is lost between the end of the hold and the best moment is the flanks'
predictions.criterion: of the interior cells dark at iteration 300 and light at iteration 504, at least 80% are flank cells; applicable only if at least 5 interior cells change from dark to light, otherwise reported as not applicable

predictions.name: P5-theStripeIsWrittenInTheHold
predictions.basis: CONTRAST with the face, whose cells darkened on the second rise; the stripe code makes the stripe even with the ring held for the whole run (S8 failed)
predictions.claim: the stripe is already dark when the ring is released
predictions.criterion: at iteration 300, at least 24 of the 27 stripe cells are dark

predictions.name: R1-theRingWritesIt
predictions.basis: face R1: >= 95% of the injected selectivity is the ring's held conductance, not the tissue-wide re-solve
predictions.claim: the clamp's ring is what writes the stripe
predictions.criterion: the ring cells' held conductances account for >= 95% of the total injected into the primary readout (sourceFlux of the selectivity readout)

predictions.name: R2-theFieldCarriesIt
predictions.basis: face R5: the field's share of the gross transfer is >= 50%
predictions.claim: the field, not the gap junctions, carries the relay
predictions.criterion: the field channel's share of the gross transfer summed over the windows from the release to the best moment is >= 0.5

predictions.name: R3-ringEndsPushIntoTheStripe
predictions.basis: the earlier code's relay (seen); CONTRAST with the face's loop through the background
predictions.claim: in flood and in clear the biggest field transfer is a ring end pushing into the nearest stripe block
predictions.criterion: in each of flood and clear the largest absolute field net transfer is positive on the pair (ringTop, stripeUpper) or the pair (ringBottom, stripeLower), that is ring top to stripe upper or ring bottom to stripe lower

predictions.name: R4-theSidesDoNotWrite
predictions.basis: the earlier code's relay and counterfactuals (seen)
predictions.claim: the ring's left side takes little part
predictions.criterion: over flood and clear, the sum of the absolute field net transfers on the pairs that include ring left is less than half the same sum over the pairs that include ring top

predictions.name: W1-theStripeFacingCellsWriteIt
predictions.basis: the earlier code (seen); CONTRAST with the face, where no 20-cell arc made the face
predictions.claim: the six ring cells above and below the stripe, held alone, write most of it
predictions.criterion: holding only the six stripe-facing ring cells (columns 4-6 of the top and bottom rows) gives a selectivity difference, against the same extraUpdateOnly baseline, of at least 50% of the full ring's, read at iteration 504

predictions.name: W2-theWallsFacingTheEndsAreTheWrite
predictions.claim: the top and bottom rows write it, the sides do not
predictions.criterion: the top and bottom rows held together give >= 75% of the full ring's selectivity difference and the left and right columns held together <= 25%

predictions.name: W3-notJustAnyCells
predictions.basis: face: size-matched random controls are the benchmark an effect has to beat
predictions.claim: the stripe-facing cells and the two walls beat equally many arbitrary ring cells
predictions.criterion: each of the six stripe-facing cells (as a set) and the top-and-bottom rows (as a set) gives a selectivity difference above the 95th percentile of 200 random subsets of the same size drawn from the ring (seed 20261001)

predictions.name: W4-bothEndsAreNeeded
predictions.basis: face: each wall half made half the lead, and neither half made a face
predictions.claim: neither end alone makes the stripe, both together do
predictions.criterion: the top row alone and the bottom row alone each leave overlap < 0.9 at iteration 504, and the top and bottom rows together reach overlap >= 0.9

predictions.name: W5-theHalvesAreAdditive
predictions.basis: face: the upper and lower wall halves added (0.370 against 0.356)
predictions.claim: the walls facing the ends and the walls facing the flanks add
predictions.criterion: the selectivity difference of the top and bottom rows alone plus that of the left and right columns alone is within 25% of the full ring's

scripts: recordBoundaryHarmonicRuns11x11.py --mode trained and computeBoundaryHarmonicBranches11x11.py then analyzeBoundaryHarmonicSwitchRule11x11.py (P1-P5, from the stripe-code summary's best codes); computeBoundaryHarmonicRelay11x11.py --baseline extraUpdateOnly --target stripesInterior --order 2 with relayLoopNets.py (V1, V3, R1-R4); analyzeBoundaryHarmonicStripeRingSegments11x11.py (W1-W5, V2).
reporting: Every criterion is reported verbatim with its number, including those that fail or reverse. P2 and P5 are contrasts with the face, written as predictions of difference. A failed W-prediction is not rescued by a different set of cells; additional sets are labelled exploratory.
